source.title: A sigh following sustained attention and mental stress: effects on respiratory variability

confidence_rationale: The only paper in this pull with an INSTRUCTED (voluntary) sigh contrasted against a spontaneous sigh and a control manoeuvre after sustained attention and mental stress. An instructed sigh restored correlated variability after arithmetic and increased total variability after sustained attention, so a deliberate respiratory act can reset a state-compressed respiratory pattern. This supports the 'voluntary sigh = deliberately forced reset' leg of MECH-109 at the respiratory level. The DV is still respiratory, not planning, and the effect was conditional ('when physiologically appropriate').
failure_signatures: The reset is demonstrated on respiratory variability only; no cognitive or planning consequence of the instructed sigh was measured.

The instructed sigh's effect depended on the preceding state (restoring correlated variability after stress, raising total variability after attention), so a voluntary sigh is not a uniform reset operator.
No voluntary breath-hold or slowed-breathing condition was tested, so only one of MECH-109's three voluntary levers (sigh) has any evidence.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Mental arithmetic and sustained attention decreased correlated and total breathing variability respectively; a spontaneous sigh restored correlated variability; an instructed sigh restored correlated variability after arithmetic and increased total variability after sustained attention.
mapping.ree_translation: A deliberately executed sigh (the MECH-109 'voluntary sigh' lever) resets the respiratory clock out of a load-compressed regime -- the respiratory precondition for a forced single-cycle plan sweep.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The reset is shown on the respiratory oscillator, not on the planning clock it is hypothesised to drive; effects are state-dependent; small lab sample; breath-hold and slow-breathing levers untested.
mapping.source_context: Healthy adults; mental arithmetic (stress) and sustained attention blocks, followed by a spontaneous sigh, an instructed sigh, or a control manoeuvre; respiratory recording.

confidence_components.notes: Only voluntary-sigh manipulation found; lifts mapping fidelity above the spontaneous-sigh papers. Vlemincx, Severs & Ramirez 2022 (Biol Psychol, PMID 35803439) review frames sighs as a state-transition 'resetting mechanism' with a stochastic-resonance account, consistent with this reading but theoretical.
